subject: Using the batch downloader for the "early-release" version of matR

messages.author: 4ad48a1892b8a420
messages.subject: Using the batch downloader for the "early-release" version of matR
parts:
I wrote a simple batch downloader that can work in conjunction with the "early-release" version of matR.
Please note that this tool is not up to production level specs.

To install the program, first paste this into R, or add it it to your .Rprofile so it is automatically loaded each time you start R:

# load function to source additional functions form github
source_https <- function(url, ...) {
  require(RCurl)
  sapply(c(url, ...), function(u) {
    eval(parse(text = getURL(u, followlocation = TRUE, cainfo = system.file("CurlSSL", "cacert.pem", package = "RCurl"))), envir = .GlobalEnv)
  })
}


# Then from R, you can use this function to source scripts directly form repositories like github. Use it now to get the batch download tool.
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DrOppenheimer/matR-apps/master/matR_batch_dl.r")

# The batch downloader is a little more primitive than matR, it directly access the API -- downloading the data for large collections of samples
# in small batches; these are merged into a single table.  With each each batch of metagenomes, a new R object and tab delimited file are written.

# Make sure that you are using the "early-release" version of matR -- instructions to uninstall other versions (if you have them), and to install
# the early release version can be found on this github page: https://github.com/MG-RAST/matR
# Follow the instructions from "To install the last stable release of matR, you can use the following commands:" to the end.

# Now you can use the batch tool to download your data
# The arguments are similar to what you use in matR, formatting is a bit different
# make sure that you have the ids for your download in a single column file, one id per line.

matR_batch_dl(mgid_list="file_with_my_ids.txt", my_annot="function", my_level="level3", my_source="Subsystems", output_prefix="some_prefix_for_output_files")

# This will allow you to download data for an unlimited number of public samples -- assuming that there are no problems with the server. Note that I strongly
# recommend using the default values for this function. If you need to access your private data, place your key in a text file (see this post for further instructions)
# and add the auth variable like this:

matR_batch_dl(mgid_list="file_with_my_ids.txt", my_annot="function", my_level="level3", my_source="Subsystems", output_prefix="some_prefix_for_output_files", auth="file_with_my_key.txt")
